name: Ice sheet / polar desert
notes: Permanent ice and polar desert (Antarctic interior, Greenland ice sheet, high-Arctic nunataks). Essentially plantless; only crustose lichens and a cushion moss survive on exposed rock edges, so the list is deliberately near-empty.

ground.name: Antarctic moss
ground.source: Bryum pseudotriquetrum, cosmopolitan moss present in Antarctic and high-Arctic rock cracks; cushions 1-5 cm (British Antarctic Survey plant lists)

traits.native_range: Bryum pseudotriquetrum, cosmopolitan moss present in Antarctic and high-Arctic rock cracks
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

ground.silhouette: low bright-green cushion on wet gravel

growth.juvenile_note: Spores or shoot fragments sprout into green protonema threads on wet gravel or seepage mud; small upright shoots with lance-shaped, red-based leaves and a strong midrib appear within weeks, then crowd into a dense turf, green above and wine-red to brown below, bound together by reddish rhizoid felt.
growth.source: Cosmopolitan moss of fens, seepages and streamsides and one of the commonest Antarctic mosses, where sporophytes are rare and shoots extend only a few mm a year; timings estimated from moss growth studies.

ground.name: Map lichen
ground.source: Rhizocarpon geographicum, bipolar/cosmopolitan crustose lichen on exposed rock incl. Antarctic nunataks; yellow-green crust <1 cm thick (Antarctic lichen flora refs)

traits.native_range: Rhizocarpon geographicum, bipolar/cosmopolitan crustose lichen on exposed rock incl
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

ground.silhouette: yellow-green crust map painted on bare rock

growth.juvenile_note: Begins as a thin black stain (prothallus) on bare, sunlit siliceous rock. Tiny angular chartreuse-yellow areoles (0.2-1.8 mm) appear on it like islands and multiply into a flat crust split by black lines, like a map; neighbouring thalli meet along black borders. Small black fruit bodies sit between the areoles. It widens by well under 1 mm a year.
growth.source: Wikipedia Rhizocarpon geographicum (patches to ~15 cm; areoles 0.2-1.8 mm; black apothecia under 1.5 mm; age estimates 9,500 yr on Baffin Island and 10,000-11,500 yr in the Brooks Range; used in lichenometry); diameter growth of roughly 0.1-1 mm/yr from lichenometry studies (knowledge)
